svg.title: SATB2-dependent gene programs in CA1 sublayer identity and inhibitory circuitry
svg.desc: Neuroday research poster. Measured RNA changes in CA1 after postnatal Satb2 deletion, gene programs, candidate intercellular signals and proposed chromatin and physiology assays.

g.text: CA1 sublayer identity and inhibitory circuitry
Mujahid Ali, Nico Wahl, Georg Dechant, Galina Apostolova
Institute for Neuroscience, Medical University of Innsbruck, Austria
When does the developing CA1 circuit need SATB2 most?
Mouse CA1 gains excitatory synapses from P14 to P21 as experience shapes its
inhibitory circuits. SATB2 helps active cortical neurons reorganize chromatin. In CA1,

text.tspan: loss strengthens PV interneuron inhibition of superficial pyramidal cells.

g.text: We predict that loss by P15 disrupts synapse organization during P15–P21
and that sublayer-specific gene-expression changes persist from P21 to P60.
RNA measured at P60 · 6 WT controls + 6 early cKO

g.title: Hippocampal nuclei, CA1 layer programs and inhibitory clusters
g.desc: Seurat classification across wild-type and Satb2 conditional knockout mice. A common stem branches into five major cell types. The excitatory branch expands into CA1 and prosubiculum cluster markers and their layer assignments. The inhibitory branch shows all original clusters with C6 divided into three SST subclusters. Each terminal cluster has its own color. Superficial and deep layer markers are ranked by paired wild-type expression. Branch widths are schematic. Hover over a marker or ribbon to read the original cluster identifier.

From Ptn expression to CA1 circuit function

text.tspan: RNA fell 52% in superficial and 36% in deep CA1.

g.title: CA1 sampling branches into nuclear profiling and acute-slice physiology
g.desc: A complete dorsal whole-brain atlas projection locates the coronal CA1 sampling plane. The RNA embedding contains all observed CA1/prosubiculum nuclei from the P60 cohort. The nuclei micrograph and fluorescence sorting gate are literature examples. The Hi-C reference is from published cortical data. Dashed routes, the separate CA1 loop model and electrophysiology denote proposed measurements.

g.title: Whole adult mouse brain with coronal sampling plane and enlarged dorsal hippocampus
g.desc: Dorsal projection of the bilateral Allen CCFv3 annotation with anterior up and CA1 projected through the translucent cerebral hemispheres. The dashed line marks the coronal plane at AP 6.95 mm from the anterior atlas origin. The adjoining atlas-based hippocampal view highlights CA1 pyramidal layer and dentate granule cell layer. Anatomical reference © Allen Institute for Brain Science.

g.title: Whole mouse brain, dorsal projection of Allen CCFv3
g.desc: Each surface location uses the first nonzero annotation along the superior-to-inferior axis. The cortex is translucent. Teal outlines show the full depth projection of CA1 in each hemisphere. The dashed line marks an atlas coronal section.

g.title: Bilateral CA1, projected through the translucent dorsal surface
g.desc: At least one Field CA1 voxel occurs anywhere along the dorsoventral column. Allen structure 382 and its children 391, 399, 407, 415 are included.

All CA1 and prosubiculum RNA coordinates, colored by five RNA-defined populations
Adapter-loaded Tn5 tags accessible DNA. The track illustrates ATAC fragment coverage across the depicted chromatin.
Investigator-supplied Tn5 illustration with Illumina sequencing adapters.
Illustrative fragment coverage across genomic position. The peak is aligned with exposed DNA between nucleosomes.
Published cortical Hi-C map and a separate schematic of a putative CA1 enhancer–promoter contact.

Published bicuculline-treated, floxed mouse primary cortical neuron Hi-C matrix, chromosome 17. The upper triangle has been reoriented with genomic position along the base and separation increasing upward. Wahl et al., 2026, Figure 7A (CC BY 4.0).
Reciprocal paired recordings in an acute hippocampal slice
g.desc: Two glass pipettes each contact a soma. Stimulation of a CA1 pyramidal cell can evoke an excitatory current in its interneuron partner. Stimulation of the interneuron can evoke an inhibitory current in the pyramidal cell.

g.data-label: Outlook for CA1 development and SATB2-associated syndrome
g.text: From CA1 circuit development to SATB2-associated syndrome
Compare each line with age-matched WT at P21 and P60. Which changes
persist in superficial and deep CA1 as the circuit matures?
Link persistent RNA changes to SATB2 binding, chromatin accessibility
Pair-record pyramidal cells with PV or SST interneurons to test whether
early loss alters excitation or inhibition in either CA1 sublayer.
during P15–P21 with restoration in adulthood (P50–P60).
